10	| Related ADRs | [ADR-0001](../../adr/0001-multi-country-content-strategy.md) (multi-country content and routes), [ADR-0002](../../adr/0002-strapi-access-and-security.md) (Strapi access and security), [ADR-0003](../../adr/0003-wizard-state-persistence.md) (wizard state persistence), [ADR-0004](../../adr/0004-forms-library.md) (forms library). All Accepted at HC2, 2026-11-20 (see §10). |
11	
12	Sources cited in this spec:
13	
14	- **Story**: [story.md](story.md).
15	- **Assessment**: the requirements that apply to every story, quoted verbatim from the assessment
16	  PDF by the orchestrator (scope rules, technical requirements, business context). They are not
17	  in the repository yet.
18	- **Skill**: the project skills `dynamic-form-fields` (FieldConfig contract v0) and
19	  `strapi-content-modeling`. This spec refines that contract; the differences are listed in §7.4.
20	- **ADR-0001..0004**: the accepted ADRs (precedence level 2, binding since HC2). Since v0.3 the
21	  spec cites them by number.
22	
23	## 1. Summary
24	
25	Step 1 of the quote wizard: a person in Colombia or Chile enters their own data and their
26	vehicle's data in a form whose fields, order, options, validations and Spanish copy all come from
27	Strapi, per country. The business team can add, remove, reorder or change fields in Strapi and
28	see the change on the next reload, with no code change and no deployment. The step blocks
29	progress while any field is invalid (vehicle year range and legal age included), and the data
30	entered is kept when the person goes to step 2 and comes back. The same build serves both
31	countries.
32	
33	## 2. Scope
34	
35	**In scope**
36	
37	- Resolving the country context for step 1 from the URL and the published country list loaded
38	  from Strapi (ADR-0001; CO and CL in the seed), the unknown-country state, and the state shown
39	  when the country list cannot be loaded.
40	- Loading the published field configuration of that country from Strapi, validating it at the
41	  boundary, ordering it, and rendering it as an accessible form with the five field types
42	  `text`, `number`, `select`, `date`, `checkbox`.
43	- Validation: required, length, numeric bounds, pattern, legal age (`minAge`), vehicle year
44	  range (`yearRange`) and, subject to US-01-Q-09, the Chilean RUT check digit.
45	- Showing the configured error message next to the field, and blocking "Continuar" while the
46	  form is invalid.
47	- Navigating to the step 2 route on a valid "Continuar", and keeping the step 1 data in the
48	  wizard state so that it is shown again when the user returns to step 1 (in-app "Atrás" and
49	  browser back), surviving a reload in the same tab (ADR-0003). In US-01 this is verified with
50	  unit tests of the store and component tests; the end-to-end part is completed in US-02
51	  (US-01-Q-19, §11).
52	- A guard that keeps step 2 unreachable while step 1 is incomplete or invalid (AC-19), and the
53	  step 2 route it protects, without a page of its own (US-01-Q-27).
54	- Loading, error and retry states for the content request.
55	- The Strapi content types for countries and form fields and the idempotent seed for CO and CL
56	  (§7, ADR-0001).
57	- The Strapi access rules (public role, published-only reads, CORS, bootstrap) and the
58	  same-origin read-only proxy through which the browser reaches the content API (ADR-0002).
59	- Keyboard-only completion, accessible labels and errors, mobile and desktop layouts.
60	
61	**Out of scope**
62	
63	- The plan list, price rule, summary, masking and payment (US-02 and US-03). This story only
64	  defines the step 1 output they consume (§7.3).
65	- Any step 2 page, provisional or final, including its heading and its "Atrás" button (US-02).
66	  No placeholder step 2 is built (US-01-Q-19 rejected at HC1).
67	- Dependent selects (for example, models filtered by make, or cities filtered by region). The
68	  vehicle model is free text (US-01-Q-21).
69	- Cross-field validation (for example, a document-number pattern that depends on the document
70	  type) (US-01-Q-11).
71	- Field types other than the five in BR-01 (email, phone, radio, textarea, file).
72	- Grouping fields into sections or sub-steps (US-01-Q-25).
73	- Normalising or reformatting values (upper-casing plates, adding dots to a RUT). Values are
74	  stored trimmed, as typed (US-01-Q-10).
75	- Countries other than CO and CL, and languages other than Spanish for end-user copy.
76	- Sending step 1 data to any server. No database (Assessment).
77	- Editor-side tooling in Strapi (preview, validation of the editor's own input beyond the schema).
78	
79	## 3. Glossary
80	
81	| Term | Meaning in this project |
82	|---|---|
83	| Country context | The country for which the wizard is running: an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code that matches a published `country` entry in Strapi (`CO` and `CL` in the seed). It is resolved from the URL path segment (`/co/…`, `/cl/…`) as decided in ADR-0001 (US-01-Q-01). |
84	| Field configuration | One published Strapi entry describing one form field for one country (§7.1). |
85	| Field key | Stable machine name of a field, unique per country (for example `documentNumber`). Used to store values and to pass them to US-02 and US-03. Never shown to the user. |
86	| Reserved key | A field key that other stories rely on (§7.3, US-01-Q-08). |
87	| Editor | A member of the business team who edits content in the Strapi admin. Non-technical. |
88	| Published | A Strapi document whose published version exists. Drafts are never visible to end users. |
89	| Wizard | The three-step flow: step 1 data (this story), step 2 plans (US-02), step 3 summary and payment (US-03). |
90	| Wizard state | The step 1 values (and later the chosen plan) held on the front end between steps, in `sessionStorage` for one country, as decided in ADR-0003 (US-01-Q-15). It holds the raw editing values; the typed step 1 output (§7.3) is produced from them only on a valid "Continuar". |
91	| Boundary validation | Checking the Strapi response against the expected contract before using it. Invalid items are dropped and logged without user data. |
92	| Today | The current local calendar date of the browser, read from an injectable clock (US-01-Q-06). |
93	| Línea (CO) | Colombian term for the vehicle model name (for example "Spark GT"). In Colombia "modelo" usually means the model **year**, so the CO seed labels follow local usage (§7.2). |
94	| Placa / Patente | Vehicle licence plate in Colombia / Chile. |
95	| RUT | Chilean national tax and identity number, with a check digit (`0–9` or `K`). |
96	
97	## 4. Business rules
98	
99	| ID | Original (source) | Refined (precise, testable) | Covered by |
100	|---|---|---|---|
101	| US-01-BR-01 | Story: "Each field is configured in Strapi with: label, type (text, number, select, date, checkbox), required flag, validations, help text, error message, order and country." | Each field configuration has: `key` (required, unique per country, see §7.1), `label` (required, non-empty), `type` (exactly one of `text`, `number`, `select`, `date`, `checkbox`), `isRequired` (boolean), `rules` (zero or more structured validation rules of the kinds in §7.1), `helpText` (optional), `errorMessage` (required, field level, used for any failure without a rule-specific message, US-01-Q-04), optional rule-specific messages, `sortOrder` (integer) and country. Only **published** configurations of the current country are rendered, sorted by `sortOrder` ascending; ties are broken by `key` ascending. A configuration that fails boundary validation is not rendered (US-01-Q-18). An empty optional field passes every rule; rules run only on non-empty values (US-01-Q-26). | US-01-AC-01, US-01-AC-02, US-01-AC-08, US-01-AC-09, US-01-AC-10, US-01-AC-14, US-01-AC-16 |
102	| US-01-BR-02 | Story: "Select fields (for example, make or city) get their options from Strapi." | A `select` field shows exactly the options configured for it in Strapi, each with `value` and `label`, in `sortOrder` ascending. No option is pre-selected; the first entry is a non-selectable prompt "Selecciona una opción" (code-owned copy, US-01-Q-14). A `select` with zero options is invalid configuration and is not rendered. The stored value is the option `value`, not its label. | US-01-AC-07, US-01-AC-14, US-01-AC-23 |
103	| US-01-BR-03 | Story: "The vehicle year cannot be later than next year or more than 20 years old." | With `Y` = the calendar year of *today*, a vehicle year `v` is valid if and only if `v` is an integer and `Y − 20 ≤ v ≤ Y + 1` (both limits inclusive). On 2026-11-20 the valid range is 2006–2027. The limits 20 and 1 are parameters of the `yearRange` rule in the configuration (seeded as 20 and 1 for both countries), so the business can change them (US-01-Q-05). | US-01-AC-05 |
104	| US-01-BR-04 | Story: "The policyholder must be of legal age." | The birth date is valid if and only if the age in completed years on *today* is ≥ the configured `minAge` (seeded as 18 for CO and for CL). A person turns N on the anniversary of their birth date; for a 29 February birth date, in non-leap years the anniversary is 1 March (US-01-Q-07). Birth dates after today are invalid. | US-01-AC-06 |
105	| US-01-BR-05 | Story context: "In Colombia the identity document is usually the citizenship ID (cédula de ciudadanía) or foreigner ID (cédula de extranjería), and the vehicle is identified by its license plate (placa). In Chile the document is the RUT and the vehicle is identified by its license plate (patente)." | CO step 1 includes a document type select with options CC "Cédula de ciudadanía" and CE "Cédula de extranjería", a document number (digits only, 6–10) and a plate labelled "Placa" (3 letters + 3 digits). CL step 1 includes a document number labelled "RUT" (with or without dots and dash, check digit `0–9`/`K`, check digit verified per US-01-Q-09) and a plate labelled "Patente" (2 letters + 4 digits, or 4 letters + 2 digits). CL has no document type field. These are **seed content**, not code; the seed is summarised in §7.2 and listed in full in the annex [seed-fields.md](seed-fields.md) (US-01-Q-03). | US-01-AC-01, US-01-AC-11, US-01-AC-12 |
106	| US-01-BR-06 | Story context: "The business team wants to add, remove or reorder fields from Strapi without asking development for changes." Assessment: "Changing a form field or a plan in Strapi must be reflected in the app without changing code." | Publishing, unpublishing or editing a field configuration (including its order, options, rules and copy) is reflected in step 1 on the next full page load of the app, with no code change, build or deployment. No browser-side or proxy cache may delay this beyond that reload (US-01-Q-16). Unpublished (draft) changes are never shown, and no anonymous caller can read them, not even by asking the content API for `status=draft` (ADR-0002). | US-01-AC-03, US-01-AC-13, US-01-AC-23, US-01-AC-28 |
107	| US-01-BR-07 | Assessment: "The same application and the same build serve Colombia and Chile." Business context: "Each country has its own regulations, identity documents, currency, coverages and copy, so the content the app consumes changes by country." | One production build serves both countries. The supported countries are the published `country` entries in Strapi, loaded once per full page load (ADR-0001); no country code, country name or country list exists in front-end code. The country context selects which content is loaded; no country-specific branch, field list or copy exists in front-end code (wizard chrome copy excepted, US-01-Q-14). A country code that is not in the loaded list shows the unknown-country state and loads no form. If the country list cannot be loaded, the root chooser and the unknown-country page show a load error with "Reintentar", never "Este país no está disponible." (ADR-0001). Data entered in one country context is never shown in the other (US-01-Q-02). | US-01-AC-01, US-01-AC-17, US-01-AC-22 |
108	| US-01-BR-08 | Assessment: "Use a front-end strategy to persist the data; a database is not required." Story AC "Keep data when going back". | Step 1 values stay in the browser: they are held in the wizard state on the front end and never sent to Strapi or any other server. They survive moving between steps (in-app and browser navigation) and a reload in the same tab; they are kept in `sessionStorage` for one country and cleared when the tab closes, when another country's context is entered and after a successful payment (ADR-0003). The store keeps the raw editing values and writes them on every change, so a reload restores exactly what was typed, valid or not (ADR-0003, HC2). Step 1 hands its values to the next steps only through the wizard state, as the typed output of §7.3, which is produced only on a valid "Continuar". | US-01-AC-04, US-01-AC-18, US-01-AC-20, US-01-AC-21, US-01-AC-27 |
109	
110	## 5. Acceptance criteria
111	
112	Conventions for every scenario:
113	
114	- Example values come from the seed (§7.2 and the annex [seed-fields.md](seed-fields.md)) and
115	  are fictitious.
116	- "Step 2" in a scenario means the step 2 route. Its page belongs to US-02 (US-01-Q-19,
117	  US-01-Q-27). Where a scenario needs that page, the note under it says what US-01 verifies and
118	  what is completed when US-02 exists.
119	- "In the context of Colombia/Chile" means the country context resolved from the URL path
120	  segment as decided in ADR-0001 (`/co/…`, `/cl/…`; step 1 at `/<country>/datos`, step 2 route
121	  at `/<country>/planes`). The scenarios do not depend on the mechanism.
122	- Where a scenario depends on *today*, the clock is pinned to the date given in the scenario.
123	- "Continuar" and "Atrás" are the step navigation buttons (code-owned copy, US-01-Q-14).
124	
125	### US-01-AC-01 — Form configured by country
126	
127	```gherkin

129	  Given the seed field configurations for Colombia and for Chile are published in Strapi
130	  When I open the application in the context of <country>
131	  Then I see exactly these field labels, in this order: <labels>
132	  And I do not see any field configured only for the other country
133	
134	  Examples:
135	    | country  | labels |
136	    | Colombia | "Tipo de documento", "Número de documento", "Nombre completo", "Fecha de nacimiento", "Ciudad", "Placa", "Marca", "Línea", "Modelo (año)", "Autorizo el tratamiento de mis datos personales." |
137	    | Chile    | "RUT", "Nombre completo", "Fecha de nacimiento", "Ciudad", "Patente", "Marca", "Modelo", "Año", "Acepto el tratamiento de mis datos personales." |
138	```
139	
140	### US-01-AC-02 — Field validation
141	
142	```gherkin

145	  And every other field holds a valid value

147	  Then I see the message "<message>" next to the field "<label>"
148	  And I cannot move to the next step: I stay on step 1 and step 2 is not shown
149

306	Note (added in v0.3, HC2 decision, ADR-0004): a `number` input whose text the browser cannot
307	parse (for example `abc` or `1e`) reaches the form model as empty (`''`), because of the HTML
308	value sanitisation rule for `<input type="number">`. The field is then handled as empty: a
309	**required** field fails the `required` check and shows its `requiredMessage` if configured,
310	otherwise its `errorMessage` (the seed's CO "Modelo (año)" has no `requiredMessage`, so the
311	field-level message is shown); an **optional** field is treated as empty, so it is valid and
312	its output is `null` (US-01-Q-26, §7.3). The app does not show a separate "not a number"
313	message. Unit tests cover the empty-value path; the CO e2e test
314	(`us-01-data-form-co.spec.ts`) confirms the sanitisation in a real browser, because jsdom does
315	not reproduce it (SPIKE-01, *Not verified* item 1).

86	### US-01-R1-F01 — Anonymous draft reads on Strapi's port (published-only middleware bypass)
87	
88	The middleware strips `status`, `publicationFilter`, `hasPublishedVersion` and `publicationState`
89	only when `ctx.path.startsWith('/api/') && !ctx.get('authorization')`. Neither condition matches
90	how Strapi authenticates or routes:
91	
92	1. **Header presence is not authentication.** Strapi's content-API strategies (API token,
93	   users-permissions JWT) only consider `Bearer <token>`. Any other `Authorization` value is
94	   ignored, the request falls back to the **public role**, and the publication parameters are
95	   kept. The comment at lines 8-11 ("an invalid one is refused with 401") is true only for
96	   `Bearer <something>`.
97	2. **The path check is case-sensitive, Strapi's router is not.** `/API/form-fields` reaches the
98	   same `find` route without passing the `/api/` test.
99	
100	Evidence, fresh `mci-review` stack (seeded draft `email` field in CO and CL), Strapi's own port:
101	
102	```
103	GET /api/form-fields?status=draft&filters[key][$eq]=email                         -> 200, data: []      (correct)
104	  + Authorization: Bearer garbage                                                  -> 401                 (correct)
105	  + Authorization: foo | Basic Zm9vOmJhcg== | Bearer | x                            -> 200, 2 drafts (ids 9, 28, publishedAt null)
106	GET /API/form-fields?status=draft&filters[key][$eq]=email   (no header at all)     -> 200, 2 drafts
107	GET /Api/form-fields?status=draft&...                       (no header at all)     -> 200, 2 drafts
108	GET /api/countries?status=draft  + Authorization: foo                              -> 200, draft countries
109	```
110	
111	Through the proxy (`:8080`) the same requests are refused: `Authorization` → 400, and `/API/…`
112	falls through to `index.html`. But ADR-0002 states that drafts stay unreadable "even when
113	someone calls Strapi's port directly", and port 1337 is published on every interface
114	(`docker-compose.yml:6`). The `status=draft` filter is the only control left on that port, and it
115	is open. This breaks BR-06 ("no anonymous caller can read them, not even by asking the content
116	API for `status=draft`") and the first AC-28 scenario. The leaked data is low-sensitivity, but the
117	AC and the ADR rule are explicit. Severity: **blocker** (security rule, AC broken).
118	
119	Expected: an anonymous request (no **valid** API token) never receives non-published content,
120	whatever its headers or path casing. Suggested direction (optional): decide on the
121	authentication result rather than the raw header, for example by forcing `status` after Strapi
122	has authenticated the request (route-level middleware or policy on the content API that checks
123	the authenticated strategy), or by rejecting unknown `Authorization` schemes. Also compare the
124	path case-insensitively. Strapi has its own `strapi::query` parsing, so re-check
125	`publicationState` and future parameters (ADR-0002 *Strongest argument against*).
126

163	### US-01-R1-F04 — Rule `value` is free JSON
164	
165	`form.validation-rule` gives `kind` an enumeration and gives `years`, `maxYearsOld` and
166	`maxYearsAhead` typed integers, but `value` (used by `minLength`, `maxLength`, `min`, `max`,
167	`pattern`) is a `json` attribute. For editors this means:
168	
169	- A pattern must be typed as a JSON string. The RUT pattern is stored as
170	  `"^[0-9]{1,2}\\.?[0-9]{3}\\.?[0-9]{3}-?[0-9kK]$"` (seed `form-fields.ts:52`). An editor who
171	  types `^\d+$` gets a JSON error, or a different regex if the escaping is wrong.
172	- A wrong type (`"tres"` for `minLength`, a number for `pattern`) saves without error, and
173	  `parseFieldConfigs` then drops the **whole field** (`field-config.ts:104`). A required reserved
174	  field such as `plate` would silently disappear from the form.
175	
176	The front end does validate at the boundary, so the app does not crash and US-01-Q-18 is met.
177	But spec §7.1 says "Rule kinds (structured, not free JSON)", and `strapi-content-modeling` says
178	editors must not be able to save something the front end cannot parse, with JSON acceptable
179	only when unavoidable. Here it is avoidable (for example a numeric `value` and a string
180	`pattern`). On open point 5: this is a real deviation, but its impact is bounded, so
181	**minor**. It needs either a schema change or a human decision recorded in the spec or ADR-0001.

Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>\n\n<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>\n\n<?claude block s1?>\n\n<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

712	## 7. Content contract (what Strapi must provide)
713	
714	This section is **logical**. The physical model is fixed by ADR-0001 and implemented by the
715	strapi-developer following `strapi-content-modeling`: a `country` collection type (`code`
716	ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 upper case, unique; `name`; `currencyCode`; `locale`; `sortOrder`; draft &
717	publish on) and a `form-field` collection type with a **required `manyToOne` relation
718	`country`**; `documents.strictRelations: true`, so an item without a country cannot be
719	published; `key` uniqueness per country enforced by a Document Service middleware (Strapi's
720	`unique` is not scoped by relation). The front end reads one country's fields in one request
721	filtered by `country.code`, and reads only published content through the same-origin proxy
722	(ADR-0002).
723	
724	### 7.1 Field configuration (per country, draft & publish on)
725	
726	| Attribute | Type | Rules |
727	|---|---|---|
728	| `key` | string | Required. `^[a-z][a-zA-Z0-9]*$`. Unique per country. Not shown to users. |
729	| `label` | string | Required, non-empty. Spanish. |
730	| `type` | enumeration | `text`, `number`, `select`, `date`, `checkbox`. |
731	| `isRequired` | boolean | Default `false`. |
732	| `helpText` | text | Optional. Spanish. |
733	| `placeholder` | string | Optional. Spanish. Never used instead of a label. |
734	| `errorMessage` | string | Required. Spanish. Field-level message (US-01-Q-04). |
735	| `sortOrder` | integer | Required. Ascending; ties by `key`. |
736	| `options` | list of { `value` string, `label` string, `sortOrder` integer } | Required and non-empty when `type` is `select`; ignored otherwise. `value` unique within the field. |
737	| `rules` | list of structured rules (below) | Zero or more, in evaluation order. Each may carry an optional `message` (Spanish) that overrides `errorMessage`. |
738	| `requiredMessage` | string | Optional. Overrides `errorMessage` for the `required` check. |
739	| `country` | required `manyToOne` relation to `country` (ADR-0001) | Exactly one country per field. Publishing without it is rejected (`strictRelations`). |
740	
741	Rule kinds (structured, not free JSON):
742	
743	| Kind | Parameters | Applies to | Semantics |
744	|---|---|---|---|
745	| `minLength` / `maxLength` | `value` integer ≥ 0 | text | Trimmed length, inclusive. |
746	| `min` / `max` | `value` number | number | Inclusive. |
747	| `pattern` | `value` ECMAScript regex source, no flags | text | Full match (anchored if not anchored). |
748	| `minAge` | `years` integer > 0 | date | BR-04. |
749	| `yearRange` | `maxYearsOld` integer ≥ 0, `maxYearsAhead` integer ≥ 0 | number | BR-03. |
750	| `rutCheckDigit` | none | text | Modulo-11 check digit, accepts dots/dash and `K`/`k` (subject to US-01-Q-09). |
751	
752	A rule whose kind does not apply to the field's type is malformed (US-01-Q-18).
753	
754	### 7.2 Seed (US-01-Q-03): summary
755	
756	The complete seed (rules, help texts, error messages, options) is in the annex
757	[seed-fields.md](seed-fields.md). Values are fictitious, copy is Spanish, and every entry is
758	published unless noted. The seed is idempotent (natural key: country code + field `key`).
759	
760	Fields per country, in `sortOrder` (key → label):
761	
762	| # | Colombia (CO), 10 published | Chile (CL), 9 published |
763	|---|---|---|
764	| 1 | `documentType` → Tipo de documento (select: CC, CE) | `documentNumber` → RUT (pattern + `rutCheckDigit`) |
765	| 2 | `documentNumber` → Número de documento | `fullName` → Nombre completo |
766	| 3 | `fullName` → Nombre completo | `birthDate` → Fecha de nacimiento (`minAge` 18) |
767	| 4 | `birthDate` → Fecha de nacimiento (`minAge` 18) | `city` → Ciudad (select) |
768	| 5 | `city` → Ciudad (select) | `plate` → Patente |
769	| 6 | `plate` → Placa | `make` → Marca (select) |
770	| 7 | `make` → Marca (select) | `model` → Modelo |
771	| 8 | `model` → Línea | `vehicleYear` → Año (`yearRange` 20 / 1) |
772	| 9 | `vehicleYear` → Modelo (año) (`yearRange` 20 / 1) | `dataConsent` → Acepto el tratamiento de mis datos personales. (checkbox) |
773	| 10 | `dataConsent` → Autorizo el tratamiento de mis datos personales. (checkbox) | — |
774	| draft | `email` → Correo electrónico (draft only, AC-13) | `email` → Correo electrónico (draft only) |
775

777	`birthDate`, `plate`, `make`, `model`, `vehicleYear`.

779	
780	### 7.3 Step 1 output (consumed by US-02 and US-03 through the wizard state)
781	
782	Two shapes exist (ADR-0003, HC2 decision). Only the second one is consumed by US-02 and US-03.
783	
784	**Stored editing values** (written on every change; what a reload restores):
785	
786	- `country`: the country code of the context (see below).
787	- `values`: a map from field `key` to the **raw editing value** of the form model, as typed:
788	  a string for `text`, `number`, `select` and `date`, a boolean for `checkbox`, and `''` for an
789	  empty field. In-progress invalid values (for example `'2015.5'`) are stored as typed. The model
790	  never holds `null` (ADR-0004).
791	
792	**Typed step 1 output** (produced only on a valid "Continuar"; never on an invalid one):
793	
794	- `country`: an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code in upper case (`^[A-Z]{2}$`) that matches a published
795	  `country` entry loaded from Strapi in this page load (ADR-0001). `CO` and `CL` are the seeded
796	  values; the type is not a fixed union of them.
797	- `values`: a map from field `key` to value. `text` → trimmed string; `number` → integer;
798	  `select` → option `value`; `date` → ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` string. An empty **optional** `text`,
799	  `number`, `select` or `date` field → `null`. `checkbox` → always a boolean: checked → `true`,
800	  unchecked → `false`, also when the checkbox is optional (HC2 decision); a checkbox is never
801	  `null`.
802	- The field configuration is **not** stored: later steps read labels and option labels from the
803	  configuration fetched in the same page load (refetched on every full page load, ADR-0003,
804	  US-01-Q-16).
805	- Reserved keys (US-01-Q-08): `documentType` (CO only), `documentNumber`, `fullName`,
806	  `birthDate`, `plate`, `make`, `model`, `vehicleYear`.

808	### 7.4 Differences from the `dynamic-form-fields` skill contract v0
809	
810	The skill says the US-01 spec may refine the contract and that the skill is updated in the same
811	PR. Differences proposed here:
812	
813	1. A required field-level `errorMessage` plus optional per-rule overrides (`requiredMessage`,
814	   rule `message`), instead of only a per-rule-kind `messages` map (US-01-Q-04).
815	2. A new rule kind `rutCheckDigit` (US-01-Q-09).
816	3. `number` fields are integers only (US-01-Q-12).
817	4. Empty optional fields skip all rules (US-01-Q-26). The skill does not state this.
818	5. Rules carry an applicability by field type (§7.1); a mismatch is malformed.

836	## 9. Non-functional requirements
837	
838	- **Accessibility (Assessment):** the step can be completed with the keyboard only (AC-24), and
839	  every field has an accessible label (AC-25). Native controls are used (`input` of type text,
840	  number, date and checkbox; `select`). Visible focus indicator. Errors are associated with their
841	  field and announced once. Target: WCAG 2.2 AA for step 1 (verified in part automatically and in
842	  part by hand at HC3, including one screen reader pass).
843	- **Responsive (Assessment):** usable from 320 to 1440 CSS px wide without horizontal scroll;
844	  verified by hand at HC3 at 360 × 740 and 1280 × 800, with screenshots as evidence (AC-26); one
845	  column; touch targets at least 24 × 24 CSS px.
846	- **Multi-country (Assessment):** one build for CO and CL; no country-specific code paths for
847	  fields or copy (BR-07).
848	- **Content-driven (Assessment, BR-06):** every field-related string, option, rule and the order
849	  come from Strapi. No field list is hard-coded in the front end.
850	- **Typed validations (Assessment):** the configuration is parsed at the boundary into a typed
851	  model (§7.1) before it reaches the form; validators are pure functions with an injectable clock.
852	- **Security / privacy (Assessment, CLAUDE.md §3):** no Strapi token with write permissions
853	  reaches the browser; the browser only reads content (AC-27). Public role permissions are
854	  minimal and justified in ADR-0002 (`find` on `country` and `form-field` only); anonymous reads
855	  return published content only, and the browser reaches the content API only through the
856	  same-origin, GET-only proxy at the relative `/api` (ADR-0002, AC-28). Step 1 values are never sent to a server or written
857	  to logs; console warnings contain no user data. Seed and test data are fictitious.
858	- **Performance:** the configuration of a country is loaded with as few requests as the content
859	  model allows (target: one), with options and rules populated in the same response. No request
860	  per keystroke. Validation runs on the client.
861	- **Environment (Assessment):** the stack starts with a single command (for example
862	  `docker compose up`) with the seed for both countries.
863	- **Language:** all end-user copy is Spanish; code, logs and docs are English.

Verification: manual, by the human at HC3, with evidence: one screenshot of step 1 of Colombia
at 360 × 740 and one at 1280 × 800, attached to the HC3 record. "Reach step 2" means the address
changes to the step 2 route (US-01-Q-27). No automated test is planned for this AC.

### US-01-AC-27 — Read-only content access, data stays in the browser (derived from US-01-BR-08 / Assessment: security)

```gherkin
Scenario: Read-only content access, data stays in the browser
  Given I complete step 1 in the context of Colombia with the values of US-01-AC-04 and reach step 2
  When I inspect every network request made by the browser during the flow
  Then every request to the content backend is a read (HTTP GET)
  And no request carries a Strapi API token with write permissions
  And no request contains any value I entered in step 1
```

"Reach step 2" means that a valid "Continuar" leads to the step 2 address (US-01-Q-27). The
requests are inspected from the first page load until that navigation.

### US-01-AC-28 — Anonymous callers cannot read drafts or write content (derived from US-01-BR-06 / ADR-0002)

New in v0.3 (HC2 decision: the ADR-0002 security check is traced as an AC).

```gherkin
Scenario Outline: Anonymous requests never return draft content
  Given the seed field "Correo electrónico" (key "email") exists for Colombia only as a draft
  When an anonymous client, without any token, requests the Colombia form fields with
    "status=draft" and "filters[key][$eq]=email" through <entry point>
  Then the response contains no field with key "email"

  Examples:
    | entry point                                 |
    | Strapi's own port (bypassing the proxy)     |
    | the same-origin proxy at the relative "/api" |

Scenario: Writes through the same-origin proxy are rejected
  When an anonymous client sends "POST /api/form-fields" through the same-origin proxy, with a
    Colombia field of key "securityProbe", type "text", label "Prueba"
  Then the response status is 405
  And an anonymous read of the Colombia form fields returns no field with key "securityProbe"
```

Verification: e2e file `us-01-security.spec.ts`, as API requests from the Playwright Node
process with no browser and no token (ADR-0002 *Confirmation*). The
check is re-run on every Strapi upgrade (ADR-0002, *Strongest argument against*).

## 7. Content contract (what Strapi must provide)

This section is **logical**. The physical model is fixed by ADR-0001 and implemented by the
strapi-developer following `strapi-content-modeling`: a `country` collection type (`code`
ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 upper case, unique; `name`; `currencyCode`; `locale`; `sortOrder`; draft &
publish on) and a `form-field` collection type with a **required `manyToOne` relation
`country`**; `documents.strictRelations: true`, so an item without a country cannot be
published; `key` uniqueness per country enforced by a Document Service middleware (Strapi's
`unique` is not scoped by relation). The front end reads one country's fields in one request
filtered by `country.code`, and reads only published content through the same-origin proxy
(ADR-0002).

### 7.1 Field configuration (per country, draft & publish on)

| Attribute | Type | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| `key` | string | Required. `^[a-z][a-zA-Z0-9]*$`. Unique per country. Not shown to users. |
| `label` | string | Required, non-empty. Spanish. |
| `type` | enumeration | `text`, `number`, `select`, `date`, `checkbox`. |
| `isRequired` | boolean | Default `false`. |
| `helpText` | text | Optional. Spanish. |
| `placeholder` | string | Optional. Spanish. Never used instead of a label. |
| `errorMessage` | string | Required. Spanish. Field-level message (US-01-Q-04). |
| `sortOrder` | integer | Required. Ascending; ties by `key`. |
| `options` | list of { `value` string, `label` string, `sortOrder` integer } | Required and non-empty when `type` is `select`; ignored otherwise. `value` unique within the field. |
| `rules` | list of structured rules (below) | Zero or more, in evaluation order. Each may carry an optional `message` (Spanish) that overrides `errorMessage`. |
| `requiredMessage` | string | Optional. Overrides `errorMessage` for the `required` check. |
| `country` | required `manyToOne` relation to `country` (ADR-0001) | Exactly one country per field. Publishing without it is rejected (`strictRelations`). |

Rule kinds (structured, not free JSON):

| Kind | Parameters | Applies to | Semantics |
|---|---|---|---|
| `minLength` / `maxLength` | `value` integer ≥ 0 | text | Trimmed length, inclusive. |
| `min` / `max` | `value` number | number | Inclusive. |
| `pattern` | `value` ECMAScript regex source, no flags | text | Full match (anchored if not anchored). |
| `minAge` | `years` integer > 0 | date | BR-04. |
| `yearRange` | `maxYearsOld` integer ≥ 0, `maxYearsAhead` integer ≥ 0 | number | BR-03. |
| `rutCheckDigit` | none | text | Modulo-11 check digit, accepts dots/dash and `K`/`k` (subject to US-01-Q-09). |

A rule whose kind does not apply to the field's type is malformed (US-01-Q-18).

### 7.3 Step 1 output (consumed by US-02 and US-03 through the wizard state)

Two shapes exist (ADR-0003, HC2 decision). Only the second one is consumed by US-02 and US-03.

**Stored editing values** (written on every change; what a reload restores):

- `country`: the country code of the context (see below).
- `values`: a map from field `key` to the **raw editing value** of the form model, as typed:
  a string for `text`, `number`, `select` and `date`, a boolean for `checkbox`, and `''` for an
  empty field. In-progress invalid values (for example `'2015.5'`) are stored as typed. The model
  never holds `null` (ADR-0004).

**Typed step 1 output** (produced only on a valid "Continuar"; never on an invalid one):

- `country`: an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code in upper case (`^[A-Z]{2}$`) that matches a published
  `country` entry loaded from Strapi in this page load (ADR-0001). `CO` and `CL` are the seeded
  values; the type is not a fixed union of them.
- `values`: a map from field `key` to value. `text` → trimmed string; `number` → integer;
  `select` → option `value`; `date` → ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` string. An empty **optional** `text`,
  `number`, `select` or `date` field → `null`. `checkbox` → always a boolean: checked → `true`,
  unchecked → `false`, also when the checkbox is optional (HC2 decision); a checkbox is never
  `null`.
- The field configuration is **not** stored: later steps read labels and option labels from the
  configuration fetched in the same page load (refetched on every full page load, ADR-0003,
  US-01-Q-16).
- Reserved keys (US-01-Q-08): `documentType` (CO only), `documentNumber`, `fullName`,
  `birthDate`, `plate`, `make`, `model`, `vehicleYear`.

### 7.4 Differences from the `dynamic-form-fields` skill contract v0

The skill says the US-01 spec may refine the contract and that the skill is updated in the same
PR. Differences proposed here:

1. A required field-level `errorMessage` plus optional per-rule overrides (`requiredMessage`,
   rule `message`), instead of only a per-rule-kind `messages` map (US-01-Q-04).
2. A new rule kind `rutCheckDigit` (US-01-Q-09).
3. `number` fields are integers only (US-01-Q-12).
4. Empty optional fields skip all rules (US-01-Q-26). The skill does not state this.
5. Rules carry an applicability by field type (§7.1); a mismatch is malformed.

## 9. Non-functional requirements

- **Accessibility (Assessment):** the step can be completed with the keyboard only (AC-24), and
  every field has an accessible label (AC-25). Native controls are used (`input` of type text,
  number, date and checkbox; `select`). Visible focus indicator. Errors are associated with their
  field and announced once. Target: WCAG 2.2 AA for step 1 (verified in part automatically and in
  part by hand at HC3, including one screen reader pass).
- **Responsive (Assessment):** usable from 320 to 1440 CSS px wide without horizontal scroll;
  verified by hand at HC3 at 360 × 740 and 1280 × 800, with screenshots as evidence (AC-26); one
  column; touch targets at least 24 × 24 CSS px.
- **Multi-country (Assessment):** one build for CO and CL; no country-specific code paths for
  fields or copy (BR-07).
- **Content-driven (Assessment, BR-06):** every field-related string, option, rule and the order
  come from Strapi. No field list is hard-coded in the front end.
- **Typed validations (Assessment):** the configuration is parsed at the boundary into a typed
  model (§7.1) before it reaches the form; validators are pure functions with an injectable clock.
- **Security / privacy (Assessment, CLAUDE.md §3):** no Strapi token with write permissions
  reaches the browser; the browser only reads content (AC-27). Public role permissions are
  minimal and justified in ADR-0002 (`find` on `country` and `form-field` only); anonymous reads
  return published content only, and the browser reaches the content API only through the
  same-origin, GET-only proxy at the relative `/api` (ADR-0002, AC-28). Step 1 values are never sent to a server or written
  to logs; console warnings contain no user data. Seed and test data are fictitious.
- **Performance:** the configuration of a country is loaded with as few requests as the content
  model allows (target: one), with options and rules populated in the same response. No request
  per keystroke. Validation runs on the client.
- **Environment (Assessment):** the stack starts with a single command (for example
  `docker compose up`) with the seed for both countries.
- **Language:** all end-user copy is Spanish; code, logs and docs are English.

712	## 7. Content contract (what Strapi must provide)
713	
714	This section is **logical**. The physical model is fixed by ADR-0001 and implemented by the
715	strapi-developer following `strapi-content-modeling`: a `country` collection type (`code`
716	ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 upper case, unique; `name`; `currencyCode`; `locale`; `sortOrder`; draft &
717	publish on) and a `form-field` collection type with a **required `manyToOne` relation
718	`country`**; `documents.strictRelations: true`, so an item without a country cannot be
719	published; `key` uniqueness per country enforced by a Document Service middleware (Strapi's
720	`unique` is not scoped by relation). The front end reads one country's fields in one request
721	filtered by `country.code`, and reads only published content through the same-origin proxy
722	(ADR-0002).
723	
724	### 7.1 Field configuration (per country, draft & publish on)
725	
726	| Attribute | Type | Rules |
727	|---|---|---|
728	| `key` | string | Required. `^[a-z][a-zA-Z0-9]*$`. Unique per country. Not shown to users. |
729	| `label` | string | Required, non-empty. Spanish. |
730	| `type` | enumeration | `text`, `number`, `select`, `date`, `checkbox`. |
731	| `isRequired` | boolean | Default `false`. |
732	| `helpText` | text | Optional. Spanish. |
733	| `placeholder` | string | Optional. Spanish. Never used instead of a label. |
734	| `errorMessage` | string | Required. Spanish. Field-level message (US-01-Q-04). |
735	| `sortOrder` | integer | Required. Ascending; ties by `key`. |
736	| `options` | list of { `value` string, `label` string, `sortOrder` integer } | Required and non-empty when `type` is `select`; ignored otherwise. `value` unique within the field. |
737	| `rules` | list of structured rules (below) | Zero or more, in evaluation order. Each may carry an optional `message` (Spanish) that overrides `errorMessage`. |
738	| `requiredMessage` | string | Optional. Overrides `errorMessage` for the `required` check. |
739	| `country` | required `manyToOne` relation to `country` (ADR-0001) | Exactly one country per field. Publishing without it is rejected (`strictRelations`). |
740	
741	Rule kinds (structured, not free JSON):
742	
743	| Kind | Parameters | Applies to | Semantics |
744	|---|---|---|---|
745	| `minLength` / `maxLength` | `value` integer ≥ 0 | text | Trimmed length, inclusive. |
746	| `min` / `max` | `value` number | number | Inclusive. |
747	| `pattern` | `value` ECMAScript regex source, no flags | text | Full match (anchored if not anchored). |
748	| `minAge` | `years` integer > 0 | date | BR-04. |
749	| `yearRange` | `maxYearsOld` integer ≥ 0, `maxYearsAhead` integer ≥ 0 | number | BR-03. |
750	| `rutCheckDigit` | none | text | Modulo-11 check digit, accepts dots/dash and `K`/`k` (subject to US-01-Q-09). |
751	
752	A rule whose kind does not apply to the field's type is malformed (US-01-Q-18).
753

780	### 7.3 Step 1 output (consumed by US-02 and US-03 through the wizard state)
781	
782	Two shapes exist (ADR-0003, HC2 decision). Only the second one is consumed by US-02 and US-03.
783	
784	**Stored editing values** (written on every change; what a reload restores):
785	
786	- `country`: the country code of the context (see below).
787	- `values`: a map from field `key` to the **raw editing value** of the form model, as typed:
788	  a string for `text`, `number`, `select` and `date`, a boolean for `checkbox`, and `''` for an
789	  empty field. In-progress invalid values (for example `'2015.5'`) are stored as typed. The model
790	  never holds `null` (ADR-0004).
791	
792	**Typed step 1 output** (produced only on a valid "Continuar"; never on an invalid one):
793	
794	- `country`: an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code in upper case (`^[A-Z]{2}$`) that matches a published
795	  `country` entry loaded from Strapi in this page load (ADR-0001). `CO` and `CL` are the seeded
796	  values; the type is not a fixed union of them.
797	- `values`: a map from field `key` to value. `text` → trimmed string; `number` → integer;
798	  `select` → option `value`; `date` → ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` string. An empty **optional** `text`,
799	  `number`, `select` or `date` field → `null`. `checkbox` → always a boolean: checked → `true`,
800	  unchecked → `false`, also when the checkbox is optional (HC2 decision); a checkbox is never
801	  `null`.
802	- The field configuration is **not** stored: later steps read labels and option labels from the
803	  configuration fetched in the same page load (refetched on every full page load, ADR-0003,
804	  US-01-Q-16).
805	- Reserved keys (US-01-Q-08): `documentType` (CO only), `documentNumber`, `fullName`,
806	  `birthDate`, `plate`, `make`, `model`, `vehicleYear`.
807	
808	### 7.4 Differences from the `dynamic-form-fields` skill contract v0
809	
810	The skill says the US-01 spec may refine the contract and that the skill is updated in the same
811	PR. Differences proposed here:
812	
813	1. A required field-level `errorMessage` plus optional per-rule overrides (`requiredMessage`,
814	   rule `message`), instead of only a per-rule-kind `messages` map (US-01-Q-04).
815	2. A new rule kind `rutCheckDigit` (US-01-Q-09).
816	3. `number` fields are integers only (US-01-Q-12).
817	4. Empty optional fields skip all rules (US-01-Q-26). The skill does not state this.
818	5. Rules carry an applicability by field type (§7.1); a mismatch is malformed.

836	## 9. Non-functional requirements
837	
838	- **Accessibility (Assessment):** the step can be completed with the keyboard only (AC-24), and
839	  every field has an accessible label (AC-25). Native controls are used (`input` of type text,
840	  number, date and checkbox; `select`). Visible focus indicator. Errors are associated with their
841	  field and announced once. Target: WCAG 2.2 AA for step 1 (verified in part automatically and in
842	  part by hand at HC3, including one screen reader pass).
843	- **Responsive (Assessment):** usable from 320 to 1440 CSS px wide without horizontal scroll;
844	  verified by hand at HC3 at 360 × 740 and 1280 × 800, with screenshots as evidence (AC-26); one
845	  column; touch targets at least 24 × 24 CSS px.
846	- **Multi-country (Assessment):** one build for CO and CL; no country-specific code paths for
847	  fields or copy (BR-07).
848	- **Content-driven (Assessment, BR-06):** every field-related string, option, rule and the order
849	  come from Strapi. No field list is hard-coded in the front end.
850	- **Typed validations (Assessment):** the configuration is parsed at the boundary into a typed
851	  model (§7.1) before it reaches the form; validators are pure functions with an injectable clock.
852	- **Security / privacy (Assessment, CLAUDE.md §3):** no Strapi token with write permissions
853	  reaches the browser; the browser only reads content (AC-27). Public role permissions are
854	  minimal and justified in ADR-0002 (`find` on `country` and `form-field` only); anonymous reads
855	  return published content only, and the browser reaches the content API only through the
856	  same-origin, GET-only proxy at the relative `/api` (ADR-0002, AC-28). Step 1 values are never sent to a server or written
857	  to logs; console warnings contain no user data. Seed and test data are fictitious.
858	- **Performance:** the configuration of a country is loaded with as few requests as the content
859	  model allows (target: one), with options and rules populated in the same response. No request
860	  per keystroke. Validation runs on the client.
861	- **Environment (Assessment):** the stack starts with a single command (for example
862	  `docker compose up`) with the seed for both countries.
863	- **Language:** all end-user copy is Spanish; code, logs and docs are English.

On 2026-11-20 the valid range is 2006–2027. The limits 20 and 1 are parameters of the `yearRange` rule in the configuration (seeded as 20 and 1 for both countries), so the business can change them (US-01-Q-05). | US-01-AC-05 |

| US-01-BR-04 | Story: "The policyholder must be of legal age." | The birth date is valid if and only if the age in completed years on *today* is ≥ the configured `minAge` (seeded as 18 for CO and for CL). A person turns N on the anniversary of their birth date; for a 29 February birth date, in non-leap years the anniversary is 1 March (US-01-Q-07). Birth dates after today are invalid. | US-01-AC-06 |

| US-01-BR-05 | Story context: "In Colombia the identity document is usually the citizenship ID (cédula de ciudadanía) or foreigner ID (cédula de extranjería), and the vehicle is identified by its license plate (placa). In Chile the document is the RUT and the vehicle is identified by its license plate (patente)." | CO step 1 includes a document type select with options CC "Cédula de ciudadanía" and CE "Cédula de extranjería", a document number (digits only, 6–10) and a plate labelled "Placa" (3 letters + 3 digits). CL step 1 includes a document number labelled "RUT" (with or without dots and dash, check digit `0–9`/`K`, check digit verified per US-01-Q-09) and a plate labelled "Patente" (2 letters + 4 digits, or 4 letters + 2 digits). CL has no document type field. These are **seed content**, not code; the seed is summarised in §7.2 and listed in full in the annex [seed-fields.md](seed-fields.md) (US-01-Q-03). | US-01-AC-01, US-01-AC-11, US-01-AC-12 |

| US-01-BR-05 | Story context: "In Colombia the identity document is usually the citizenship ID (cédula de ciudadanía) or foreigner ID (cédula de extranjería), and the vehicle is identified by its license plate (placa). | Boundary validation | Checking the Strapi response against the expected contract before using it. Invalid items are dropped and logged without user data. |
| Wire shape / logical shape | The *wire shape* is the JSON that the Strapi 5 REST API returns, with Strapi's attribute names (for example a rule's `pattern`, a country's `localeTag`). The mapping between the two is stated in §7.5 (added in v0.4). |
| Anonymous request | Any request to the content API that Strapi does not authenticate with a valid token: no `Authorization` header, a scheme other than `Bearer` (`foo`, `Basic …`), `Bearer` with no token, or an invalid token, on any letter case of the `/api` path, on Strapi's own port or through the proxy (added in v0.4, US-01-R1-F02). |

input.new_string:
5. Rules carry an applicability by field type (§7.1); a mismatch is malformed.
6. (v0.4, US-01-R1-F04) On the wire, a rule has one typed attribute per parameter type
   (`value` number, `pattern` text, `years`, `maxYearsOld`, `maxYearsAhead` integers); no
   free-JSON attribute. The logical `ValidationRule` is unchanged (§7.5).

### 7.5 Wire shapes (Strapi 5 REST) and mapping to the logical shape (v0.4)

Added in v0.4 after code review round 1 (US-01-R1-F04, US-01-R1-F05; human decisions of
2026-11-21; physical model in ADR-0006, which amends ADR-0001's physical model). The developers
implement the backend to return exactly these shapes, and the front-end boundary parser
(`field-config.ts`, `country.ts`) maps them to the logical shapes. The test-engineer derives the
parser fixtures from them.

#### 7.5.1 Validation rule (`form.validation-rule` component, inside a form field's `rules`)

Every rule on the wire carries **all** of the attributes below. The attributes its kind does not
use are `null`. Strapi adds the component `id`, which the parser ignores.

| Wire attribute | JSON type on the wire | Used by kind(s) | Editor input (Strapi admin) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kind` | string, one of `minLength`, `maxLength`, `min`, `max`, `pattern`, `minAge`, `yearRange`, `rutCheckDigit` | all | enumeration (required) |
| `value` | number or `null` | `minLength`, `maxLength`, `min`, `max` | numeric input |
| `pattern` | string or `null` | `pattern` | plain text input: the regex is typed as is (`^\d+$`), with no JSON quoting or doubled backslashes |
| `years` | integer or `null` | `minAge` | integer input |
| `maxYearsOld` | integer or `null` | `yearRange` | integer input |
| `maxYearsAhead` | integer or `null` | `yearRange` | integer input |
| `message` | string or `null` | all (optional override, US-01-Q-04) | text input |

The Strapi attribute types (for example `integer` versus `decimal` for `value`, `string` versus
`text` for `pattern`) and their schema-level minimums are fixed in ADR-0006; whatever they are,
the JSON types above hold. Every current use of `value` is an integer (lengths, and bounds of
integer-only `number` fields, US-01-Q-12).

Examples (wire), as returned inside `data[i].rules` of `GET /api/form-fields`:

```json
{ "id": 41, "kind": "pattern",   "value": null, "pattern": "^[A-Za-z]{3}[0-9]{3}$", "years": null, "maxYearsOld": null, "maxYearsAhead": null, "message": null }
{ "id": 42, "kind": "minLength", "value": 3,    "pattern": null, "years": null, "maxYearsOld": null, "maxYearsAhead": null, "message": "Ingresa tu nombre completo (entre 3 y 80 caracteres)." }
{ "id": 43, "kind": "minAge",    "value": null, "pattern": null, "years": 18,   "maxYearsOld": null, "maxYearsAhead": null, "message": null }
{ "id": 44, "kind": "yearRange", "value": null, "pattern": null, "years": null, "maxYearsOld": 20,   "maxYearsAhead": 1,    "message": null }
{ "id": 45, "kind": "rutCheckDigit", "value": null, "pattern": null, "years": null, "maxYearsOld": null, "maxYearsAhead": null, "message": null }
```

(The values are illustrative; the seed values are in [seed-fields.md](seed-fields.md).)

Mapping wire → logical `ValidationRule` (§7.1), applied per rule by the boundary parser:

| Wire `kind` | Parameter read from the wire | Valid when | Logical rule produced |
|---|---|---|---|
| `minLength`, `maxLength` | `value` | a JSON number, integer, ≥ 0 | `{ kind, value }` |
| `min`, `max` | `value` | a JSON number, finite | `{ kind, value }` |
| `pattern` | `pattern` | a non-empty JSON string that compiles as an ECMAScript regex with no flags | `{ kind: 'pattern', value: <pattern> }` |
| `minAge` | `years` | a JSON number, integer, > 0 | `{ kind: 'minAge', years }` |
| `yearRange` | `maxYearsOld`, `maxYearsAhead` | both JSON numbers, integers, ≥ 0 | `{ kind: 'yearRange', maxYearsOld, maxYearsAhead }` |
| `rutCheckDigit` | none | always | `{ kind: 'rutCheckDigit' }` |

Rules of the mapping:

1. The logical `ValidationRule` of §7.1 is unchanged: the logical `pattern` rule keeps its
   regex in `value`, so validators and their tests do not change. Only the parser reads a
   different wire attribute for `pattern`.
2. `message`: a non-empty string becomes the logical `message`; `null`, an empty or a blank
   string means "no override".
3. Attributes the kind does not use are **ignored**, whatever their value (an editor who
   changes a rule's kind may leave a stale value behind). They are `null` in the seed.
4. A rule is **malformed** when its `kind` is unknown, does not apply to the field's type
   (§7.1), or the parameter its kind reads is missing, `null`, of the wrong JSON type (numeric
   text such as `"3"` is a wrong type) or out of range. A malformed rule makes its field
   malformed: the field is dropped with a `console.warn` naming the field key and the problem,
   with no user data (US-01-Q-18, AC-14).

#### 7.5.2 Country (`country` collection type)

The API exposes the stored attribute name **`localeTag`**, with no renaming in the backend (no
custom controller mapping `fields`, `sort` or `filters`; human decision on US-01-R1-F05). It can
therefore be selected, sorted and filtered as `localeTag` like any other attribute. The front end
requests it by that name (for example `fields[3]=localeTag`), never as `locale`.

Example (wire), `GET /api/countries?fields[0]=code&fields[1]=name&fields[2]=currencyCode&fields[3]=localeTag&fields[4]=sortOrder&sort=sortOrder:asc`
(published content only, ADR-0002):

```json
{
  "data": [
    { "id": 1, "documentId": "…", "code": "CO", "name": "Colombia", "currencyCode": "COP", "localeTag": "es-CO", "sortOrder": 10 },
    { "id": 2, "documentId": "…", "code": "CL", "name": "Chile",    "currencyCode": "CLP", "localeTag": "es-CL", "sortOrder": 20 }
  ],
  "meta": { "pagination": { "page": 1, "pageSize": 25, "pageCount": 1, "total": 2 } }
}
```

(`id`, `documentId` and `meta` are added by Strapi and ignored by the parser. The `sortOrder`
values are those of the current seed.)

Mapping wire → logical country entry (the front-end `Country` model):

| Wire attribute | Valid when | Logical attribute |
|---|---|---|
| `code` | a string matching `^[A-Z]{2}$` | `code` |
| `name` | a non-empty string | `name` |
| `currencyCode` | a string matching `^[A-Z]{3}$` | `currencyCode` |
| `localeTag` | a non-empty string | `locale` |
| `sortOrder` | a JSON number | `sortOrder` |

The logical attribute keeps the name `locale` (it is the BCP 47 tag that US-02 and US-03 use for
number and currency formatting); only the boundary parser knows the wire name `localeTag`. An
entry that fails any row is dropped with a `console.warn` that carries no content (ADR-0001). A
wire entry with `locale` but no `localeTag` is invalid.

Also: new glossary entry *Wire shape / logical shape*; sources list adds Review R1. No ID renumbered or retired; no ID added. ## Spec v0.4 written

I revised `/Users/cristiansabogal/Proyectos/multicountry-car-insurance/specs/US-01/spec.md` from v0.3 to **v0.4**. Status is "Draft — awaiting HC1 (round 4)", and the "Approved by" field reads "v0.4: pending". `tasks.md` is untouched, as you asked. Nothing was committed, pushed or switched.

**Counts:** 8 BR, 28 AC (4 original, 24 derived), 28 Q. No IDs were added, renumbered or retired, no Human answer cells or earlier Review log rows were touched, and no Q blocks HC1.

**ADRs needed:** only ADR-0006 (amends ADR-0001's physical model). It is cited in the metadata, in §7 and as in progress in §10. The spec states that ADR-0001 still names the attribute `locale` until ADR-0006 is accepted.

### What changed, by section and ID
- **Metadata and sources:** version, status and ADR-0006 in Related ADRs. The sources list now includes Review R1 (`reviews/US-01-review-R1.md`).
- **§3 Glossary:** two new entries.
  - "Wire shape / logical shape".
  - "Anonymous request": any request Strapi does not authenticate. That covers no header, a non-Bearer scheme, `Bearer` with no token, an invalid token, and any letter case of `/api`, on Strapi's port or through the proxy.
- **US-01-BR-06:** "no anonymous caller" now points to the glossary definition.
- **US-01-BR-07:** the chrome-copy exception points to §8.1.
- **US-01-AC-14:** two new Examples rows and a note.
  - A pattern rule with `"pattern"` null and its regex in `"value"`.
  - A minLength rule whose `"value"` is the text `"3"` instead of a number.
- **US-01-AC-28 (ID kept, widened for F02):**
  - The draft outline now has 14 rows: 7 variants (no header, `foo`, `Basic Zm9vOmJhcg==`, `Bearer` with no token, `Bearer not-a-real-token`, `/API/`, `/Api/`) on each of Strapi's port and the proxy. It also checks that every returned entry has a non-null `publishedAt`.
  - A new outline covers draft countries (5 rows).
  - A note says a 400, a 401 or a non-API answer (such as `index.html`) satisfies `Then`. The same rows must also be run with `publicationFilter`, `hasPublishedVersion` and `publicationState` in place of `status=draft`.
  - The write scenario is unchanged.
- **§7:**
  - The intro names the country attribute `localeTag` and cites "ADR-0006 (amends ADR-0001's physical model)".
  - The §7.1 rule-kinds preamble points to §7.5.
  - §7.4 gets a new item 6.
  - The new **§7.5** holds the wire shapes and the wire-to-logical mapping.
- **§8:** a new *Country chooser* row, and a new **§8.1** that lists all code-owned copy. It collects the Q-14 and Q-28 strings (their cells are unchanged) and adds "Elige tu país" (chooser heading) and "Cotizador de seguro de auto" (page `<title>`), both marked "Approved at review round 1 (F06)".
- **§10:** ADR-0006 is listed as in progress.
- **§11:** the e2e table row for AC-28 and the AC-14, AC-17 and AC-28 mapping rows are updated. There are still exactly 4 e2e files.
- **§13:** a new v0.4 row lists each change with its source (US-01-R1-F04, F05, F06, F02 and the human decision of 2026-11-21).

### Wire shape of a rule (§7.5.1)
A rule arrives in `data[i].rules` of `GET /api/form-fields`. Every rule carries all of these attributes, and the ones its kind does not use are `null`:

```json
{ "id": 41, "kind": "pattern", "value": null, "pattern": "^[A-Za-z]{3}[0-9]{3}$", "years": null, "maxYearsOld": null, "maxYearsAhead": null, "message": null }
```

| Attribute | JSON type | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| `kind` | string enum | all |
| `value` | number or null | minLength, maxLength, min, max |
| `pattern` | string or null | pattern (editors type the regex as is) |
| `years` | integer or null | minAge |
| `maxYearsOld`, `maxYearsAhead` | integer or null | yearRange |
| `message` | string or null | all |

The `id` is ignored. ADR-0006 fixes the Strapi attribute types (for example integer or decimal); the JSON types above hold either way.

**Mapping to the logical `ValidationRule`.** The §7.1 shape does not change, so the validators do not change.

| Wire kind | Valid when | Logical rule |
|---|---|---|
| minLength / maxLength | `value` is an integer ≥ 0 | `{kind, value}` |
| min / max | `value` is a finite number | `{kind, value}` |
| pattern | `pattern` is a non-empty string that compiles | `{kind:'pattern', value: pattern}` |
| minAge | `years` is an integer > 0 | `{kind:'minAge', years}` |
| yearRange | both attributes are integers ≥ 0 | `{kind:'yearRange', maxYearsOld, maxYearsAhead}` |
| rutCheckDigit | always | `{kind:'rutCheckDigit'}` |

- **Message:** a non-empty `message` becomes the override. `null` or a blank string means no override.
- **Unused attributes:** they are ignored whatever their value.
- **Malformed rule:** an unknown kind, a kind that does not apply to the field type, or a parameter that is missing, null, of the wrong JSON type or out of range. Numeric text such as `"3"` counts as the wrong type. The whole field is then dropped with a `console.warn` naming the key and the problem (AC-14).

### Wire shape of a country (§7.5.2)
Example request: `GET /api/countries?fields[0]=code&fields[1]=name&fields[2]=currencyCode&fields[3]=localeTag&fields[4]=sortOrder&sort=sortOrder:asc`

```json
{ "id": 1, "documentId": "…", "code": "CO", "name": "Colombia", "currencyCode": "COP", "localeTag": "es-CO", "sortOrder": 10 }
```

- The backend exposes `localeTag` with no renaming. It needs no custom controller for `fields`, `sort` or `filters`, so it works in all three like any other attribute.
- The parser maps `code` (`^[A-Z]{2}$`), `name` (non-empty), `currencyCode` (`^[A-Z]{3}$`), `localeTag` (non-empty string) → logical **`locale`**, and `sortOrder` (number).
- An entry that has `locale` but no `localeTag` is invalid and is dropped with a warning.

### Impact on the current code
- **Backend:** in `backend/src/components/form/validation-rule.json`, `value` changes from json to a numeric type and a new `pattern` attribute is needed. The custom `backend/src/api/country/controllers/country.ts` (the `locale` mapping) goes away. The seed moves patterns into `pattern`, and the seed comments in `backend/src/seed/countries.ts` should be updated.
- **Frontend:**
  - `frontend/src/app/shared/field-config.ts` must read `pattern` from the wire. Its `num()` currently accepts numeric text, which the spec now treats as malformed.
  - `frontend/src/app/shared/country.ts` must read `localeTag` and require it to be non-empty. Today it reads `locale` and accepts any string.
  - `frontend/src/app/core/country-content-api.ts` must request `fields[3]=localeTag`.
- **Tests:** the test-engineer needs the two new AC-14 rows, the 19 AC-28 rows and a unit test for the country parser. That parser test is unmapped today, because `frontend/src/app/shared/` has no spec file for `country.ts`.
